findings.title: Listener gated by V1 feature flag disables cleanup in V2
findings.body: The new `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ))` wraps the entire event body, so when only the V2 feature (`ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2`) is enabled the `RoleRemovedEvent`, `ClientRemovedEvent` and `GroupRemovedEvent` handlers are skipped entirely. Previously the handlers ran unconditionally, and `MgmtPermissionsV2.roles()` still has a real `setPermissionsEnabled` implementation that is no longer invoked, so role/group permission state will be left orphaned when those entities are removed in a V2-only realm. The check should be `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ || ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2`, or the per-handler calls must selectively skip the V2-unsupported `ClientPermissions.setPermissionsEnabled`.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission returns the literal string "Clients" as a client id
findings.body: `getClientsWithPermission` iterates every resource whose type is "Clients", which includes the schema's "all-clients" resource (created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init` with name="Clients" and type="Clients"). If the all-clients resource has the requested scope granted, `hasGrantedPermission` returns true and the string `"Clients"` is added to the returned set. The contract of the method is a set of client ids; returning `"Clients"` causes callers (e.g. code that filters `realm.clients().get(...)`) to either crash trying to look up a client with that id or silently behave as if no clients matched. The handler must skip the resource whose name equals `CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE` (and, when that resource is granted, return the set of all client ids in the realm, not the literal "Clients").

findings.title: Potential NPE when all-clients resource does not exist
findings.body: In `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`, when the per-client resource is null the code calls `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)`. That method returns null when admin permissions are disabled, when the type is unknown, or when the resource was never created. The next line then calls `authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource)` with a null resource, which will NPE inside the policy store. The fallback path must null-check the result of `getResourceTypeResource` and return `false` when null.

findings.title: getResourceName has no case for the Clients resource type
findings.body: `getResourceName` special-cases the `USERS` resource type (translating the all-users marker to "All users" and otherwise looking up the user to return the username). For the new `CLIENTS` resource type the method falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`, so client-typed resources will be displayed as the client UUID (the stored name) instead of a friendly label, and the all-clients resource will appear as the literal string "Clients" rather than "All clients". A symmetric branch for `CLIENTS.getType()` should be added.

findings.title: Unused method and dead imports
findings.body: `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken)` is defined but never referenced from anywhere in the class. The accompanying imports (`ClientModelIdentity`, `DefaultEvaluationContext`, `EvaluationContext`, `AccessToken`) and the `TOKEN_EXCHANGE` static import are also dead. The unused `logger` field is declared on line 51 as well. This is dead code introduced together with the new class and should be removed.

findings.title: testManageOnlyOneClient assumes at least 2 default client scopes
findings.body: After granting `MANAGE`, the test does `ClientScopeRepresentation clientScopeRep = defaultClientScopes.get(1);` (and again on line 174). If the realm configuration registers fewer than two default client scopes for `myclient` (the realm-admin permissions config in this PR adds new scopes that are stored on the admin-permissions client, not on the application client), `get(1)` throws IndexOutOfBoundsException and the test fails for reasons unrelated to the authorization logic. The test should either assert `defaultClientScopes.size() >= 2` or iterate by content rather than by hard-coded index.

findings.title: No test exercises canMapClientScopeRoles, canManageClientScopes or canView(ClientScopeModel)
findings.body: ClientPermissionsV2 implements `canMapClientScopeRoles` (backed by `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE`), `canManageClientScopes` (backed by the `MANAGE` scope) and `canView(ClientScopeModel)` (backed by `VIEW`/`MANAGE`), but PermissionClientTest only covers `MANAGE`, `CONFIGURE`, `VIEW`, `MAP_ROLES` and `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE`. The `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` scope is registered in the schema but is not exercised by any test, leaving the new authorization logic uncovered. A test mirroring `testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient` should grant `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` and verify that client-scope role mappings can and cannot be performed.
